issue_context.title: Pull Request counter offset after deleting branch
issue_context.body:
### Description

possibly related to #19190

Unfortunately not able to reproduce.

Multiple PRs were based on a branch, which also had a PR to the master branch. upon closing the PR to the master branch and deleting the underlying branch, the other PRs were automatically closed. so far so good, but the pull request counter is not permanently off by 1. 

See screenshots.

Right now there are two PRs open but the counter says 2. If no pull requests are open, it says `-1` which is extra fun

### Gitea Version

1.15.11

### Can you reproduce the bug on the Gitea demo site?

No

### Log Gist

_No response_

### Screenshots

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/58218546/162457520-a2216a83-88ca-4f1e-8850-e0786a7c4416.png)


### Git Version

_No response_

### Operating System

alpine

### How are you running Gitea?

from openRC

### Database

PostgreSQL

review_comments: is this the intended usage? to use builder eq for an update statement?!?

What is going on here is that the builder is misused to set the field to update dynamically.
But yeah, maybe we should document this line as I've also struggled with it, and it certainly isn't as apparent as is typical for Go code.
for my understanding `builder.Eq{field: subQuery}` is equivalten to go-code `fmt.Sprintf("%s = %s", field, subQuery)` but better sanitized
Here Update means Set and Update
@lunny can you add some code comment to explain for others :)
Done. And in fact, this is not the first place we use `builder.Update` in codebase.

Yeah, I can absolutely understand why the syntax highlighter is absolutely confused.
Got me as well for a minute.
